definitions.explanation: To apply a new coat of paint over an existing surface; to change the color by repainting.
(Figurative) To replace an existing record or history with a new one; to set a new record.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}を{白|しろ}く{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}えた。
{古|ふる}くなった{外壁|がいへき}を{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}える{時期|じき}だ。
examples.english: It's time to repaint the old exterior walls.

examples.japanese: {世界記録|せかいきろく}を{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}えた。
{歴史|れきし}を{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}える{大発見|だいはっけん}だ。
examples.english: This is a great discovery that will rewrite history.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Compound verb: {塗|ぬ}る + {替|か}える.

PATTERN: Xを{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}える (repaint X / rewrite X)

COMPOUND VERB PATTERN: ～{替|か}える compounds indicate replacing or redoing:
・{書|か}き{替|か}える (to rewrite)
・{作|つく}り{替|か}える (to remake)
・{入|い}れ{替|か}える (to replace)

FIGURATIVE USE: Very common in sports journalism when describing record-breaking achievements.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{記録|きろく}を{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}える (break a record)
・{歴史|れきし}を{塗|ぬ}り{替|か}える (rewrite history)
